challenges.question: State the current train-first/private-car transport hierarchy and point to one concrete piece of live INDIA20/INDIA21 work where it was actually applied, not merely known.
challenges.start_session_answer: The hierarchy (CURRENT_DECISIONS_MASTER.md sec.4 / MRK-028): train first when practical, target 1A, domestic flight only for real door-to-door time savings, private car for mountains/last-mile, no long-distance bus, and every edge must count checkout/loading/wait/security/baggage/onward/check-in/rest/daylight, not raw timetable time. Concrete application already on record: the Bodh Gaya -> Varanasi outbound edge uses train 20887 Vande Bharat Express (decisions/BODHGAYA_CLUSTER_CLOSURE_MARK_DECISION_2026-08-29.md), not a private car, even though a car would also work, because train-first controls when practical. Conversely, INDIA20's Dec 23 Kumaon transfer (Nainital -> Vivekananda detours -> Dunagiri/Kukuchina) correctly uses one prebooked private driver, because this is exactly the mountain/last-mile case where the hierarchy prescribes a car, not a train. I did not introduce any new transport-mode decision this session, so my own compliance test is negative: the live-ledger sync repair and INDIA20 extraction touched zero transport-mode content, so there was nothing to get wrong here, but I did verify neither artifact silently proposed a car where a train edge was already locked.
challenges.checker_evidence: governance/CURRENT_DECISIONS_MASTER.md sec.4 (train-first hierarchy); decisions/BODHGAYA_CLUSTER_CLOSURE_MARK_DECISION_2026-08-29.md line ~53 (20887 Vande Bharat Express as the outbound edge); decisions/INDIA20_DEC23_24_KUMAON_VIVEKANANDA_TRANSIT_AND_BABAJI_DAY_MARK_DECISION_2026-09-13.md (private driver for the Dec 23 mountain transfer). Verified both citations are real, existing files with the stated content.

challenges.question: Before writing the INDIA20 extraction, you found six-plus candidates framed as 'still OPEN' in CURRENT_STATE.md. Show exactly how you determined they were actually already decided rather than presenting them to Mark as fresh choices.
challenges.start_session_answer: I did not trust either the 'still OPEN' framing in CURRENT_STATE.md or the CSV's OPEN grade at face value. For each of Kasar Devi Cave, Vivekananda Ancestral House, Cossipore Udyanbati, Balaram Mandir, Shyampukur Bati and the Chennai Vivekananda House, I ran `git log -S` against the live ledger CSV to find the exact commit that changed each row away from OPEN, then read that commit's accompanying decisions/*.md file in full. Two of those files (decisions/INDIA20_KAKRIGHAT_AMHERST_DIHIKA_RICH_LOCATION_CARD_MARK_DECISIONS_2026-09-13.md and decisions/INDIA20_KOLKATA_VIVEKANANDA_PRIORITY_AND_CHENNAI_BYCATCH_MARK_DECISION_2026-09-13.md) explicitly state their own supersede relationship ('Mark decision supersedes the prior provisional C-under-current-route treatment'; 'Mark clarified the numbered set... The earlier mapping in this file is superseded'). Only after confirming a genuine Mark decision existed and postdated the OPEN framing did I write the grades into the extraction and fix the CSV/CURRENT_STATE.md — I did not re-present any of the six to Mark, and I did not decide anything myself; I only made the mechanical record agree with Mark's own already-recorded decision.

I resolved the CURRENT_STATE.md/live-ledger disagreement by tracing each candidate to its authoritative, most-recent decision file via git history and rewriting CURRENT_STATE.md's section to state the resolved grades and cite the fix. After that repair, all three files agree: CURRENT_STATE.md and INDIA_CURRENT_KNOWLEDGE_MAP.md both correctly point to the live ledger CSV as current truth and both now correctly treat only Lala Badri Shah House and J.C. Bose as genuinely open in that family; CURRENT_DECISIONS_MASTER.md's coarser framing (still-open Bodh/Tiru duration ballot, live-ledger/v4 repair as the current global process) is not contradicted by either.

challenges.question: Identify one specific FOUT from governance/MARK_TO_INDIA_SUCCESSOR_HUMAN_HANDOFF.md that is materially relevant to what you actually did this session, state the required solution, show current-source evidence of where the risk arose, and demonstrate concretely how your actual work complied.
challenges.start_session_answer: FOUT 24 (POST-BOOT RICH-SOURCE ACTIVATION) is the directly relevant one: it warns that a successor can pass a valid boot and even a compact reconciliation and still act on an impoverished summary that hides real WHY/status, and its required solution is to open the owning/raw source layers behind a compact card BEFORE using it, especially before recommending a downgrade or treating something as unresolved. The risk arose concretely in CURRENT_STATE.md's own compact 'HIGH-PRIORITY RECOVERED OPEN CANDIDATES' section: it read as a clean, plausible current-state summary, and a successor trusting it at face value would have re-presented six already-decided candidates to Mark as if they were still his open choice — precisely the kind of successor failure this file exists to prevent, and precisely the kind of mistake Mark has reacted to with real anger earlier in this project (the Manikarnika/Lahiri Mahasaya miss) when a compact/summary layer hid a real fact. I complied by not trusting the compact CURRENT_STATE.md wording, opening the actual decisions/*.md files behind each of the six candidates via git history, and confirming the true current grade before writing anything into the extraction — the same FOUT-24 discipline the handoff requires, applied to this session's actual first substantive task rather than merely cited from memory.
challenges.checker_evidence: governance/MARK_TO_INDIA_SUCCESSOR_HUMAN_HANDOFF.md FOUT 24 section (full text, 'VERPLICHTE OPLOSSING — POST-BOOT RICH-SOURCE ACTIVATION', points 1-10); governance/CURRENT_STATE.md pre-repair 'HIGH-PRIORITY RECOVERED OPEN CANDIDATES' section (the impoverished summary that would have misled a successor); decisions/CCI_LIVE_LEDGER_SYNC_REPAIR_2026-09-13.md (the actual raw-source-tracing work performed). All three inspected; the FOUT text, the risk instance, and the compliance action all verified consistent with the answer.
